children: Oil prices are lower in early Asian trade as the market tracks developments in the Middle East. America's Gulf allies are steeling themselves for a U.S. bombardment of Iran while the Trump administration and Arab mediators are making efforts to reach a negotiated end to the conflict. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian has said Tehran is willing to continue talks. Still, ANZ analysts note that the oil market is wary of "stop-and-go diplomatic efforts that haven't delivered peace, with the two adversaries yet to agree on terms for fully reopening the Strait of Hormuz."Front-month West Texas Intermediate crude-oil futures are down 0.1% at $96.35 a barrel, while front-month Brent is 8.0% lower at $104.32 a barrel. (sherry.qin@wsj.com)
